context.task: Classify a real final native-install smoke-check failure before FileBlade 0.2.0 release
facts: A fresh installation under a 112-byte canonical authority socket path installs and prints its version, but native roles disable and owned removal fail with the actual error path must be shorter than SUN_LEN. No live authority exists in that profile.

The shared authority transport connects to canonical_root/authority.sock and the native server binds that same pathname. Both use the Unix pathname address field, which cannot contain this otherwise valid XDG state path.

All consumers already share transport::connect. Linux can resolve /proc/self/fd/<open-directory-fd>/authority.sock within the same owned directory; its short address preserves the same physical socket, permissions, kernel lock and state namespace. The open descriptor is retained for the bind/connect call. Existing authority ownership and identity checks remain.

A real integration test already starts the actual native authority, sends public CLI reads/writes and checks refusal after stop. Giving it a long home directory and checking offline role reversal covers server bind, shared client routing and cleanup without mocks.

The final public source identity is not published. The user asked to fix every found issue immediately. Updating the shared transport/server and rebuilding the final artifact can close this concrete regression before handoff.
